audience_note: Describes the police shooting of unarmed protesters, including people shot from behind; casualty figures are disputed.
author: historian-agent:o-s15
title: Sebokeng police shooting of protesters, 26 March 1990
summary: On 26 March 1990 police opened fire on a crowd of roughly 50,000 marching in Sebokeng, in the Vaal region south of Johannesburg, killing and wounding many marchers, a number of them shot from behind. A commission under Richard Goldstone found the force excessive. Reported death tolls range from five to seventeen, and ANC-government talks were called off.

uncertainty.note: Date is firm; casualty figures differ: Goldstone five dead and 161 wounded; Human Rights Watch 17 dead; the TRC report 13 dead and over 400 injured (second-hand).

as_recorded.value: On March 26, initial talks between the government and the ANC were called off after 17 black protesters were killed (1990 report)

where.historical_name: Sebokeng township, Lekoa area, Transvaal Province, Republic of South Africa

importance.justification: A mass police shooting weeks after Mandela's release that suspended early ANC-government talks and was examined by the Goldstone inquiry.

sources.title: Sebokeng, 26 March 1990 (O'Malley Archive, The Heart of Hope)
sources.author: Padraig O'Malley

sources.title: Human Rights Watch World Report 1990: South Africa

reviewer_note: Least sure of the casualty counts: the O'Malley page gives Goldstone's five dead and 161 wounded and notes other tallies; HRW says 17 dead. The TRC volume page could not be opened, so TRC figures are second-hand via O'Malley. The sequence of the first shots is only briefly summarized.
